title: Restricted-child protected-state isolation qualification
objective: Qualify the COTRA-P05 protected-state boundary on native Windows before broader execution authority is introduced: a zero-capability AppContainer child must be unable to read Cotra-owned protected state outside the trusted workspace, must receive no Cotra/tunnel secret material or privileged authority handles, and any failure to prove isolation must block successor authority widening.

include: provider-private native Windows protected-state read-denial fixture
Cotra-owned protected-state sentinel under the parent user's LocalAppData Cotra state boundary
verification that the restricted child cannot read protected sentinel contents
verification that Cotra/tunnel secret-like environment variables remain absent from the child environment
verification that child handle inheritance remains limited to NUL stdin plus dedicated stdout/stderr handles
verification that the current cotra-mcp to cotrad stdio authority channel is not inherited by process.spawn children
fail-closed qualification if native Windows permits the protected-state read
minimal Cotra-owned state ACL hardening if and only if native evidence proves the inherited Windows ACL boundary insufficient
SG-000009, SG-000009A, SG-000010, and SG-000011 regression coverage
exclude: changing ACLs on user workspaces or arbitrary user-provided files
approval bypass or persistent approval reuse

authority_delta.filesystem: No public filesystem authority. Qualification may harden Cotra-owned protected state only; trusted workspace ACLs and arbitrary user files remain untouched.
authority_delta.process: No new public process authority; provider-private isolation qualification only
authority_delta.secrets: No new secret access; this grain proves restricted-child non-access to Cotra-owned protected state and preserves secret-free child environments

invariants: Windows public process.spawn remains restricted to the exact SG-000010-qualified System32 whoami.exe target
A restricted child must not be able to read Cotra-owned protected-state sentinel contents outside the trusted workspace
A successful process result must never be used as evidence that protected-state isolation exists; isolation requires a dedicated negative-access proof
Cotra/tunnel secret-like environment variables remain absent from every contained child
The child inherits only NUL stdin and its dedicated stdout/stderr pipe writers through the explicit handle list
The cotra-mcp to cotrad authority channel is not an inheritable child authority surface in the current stdio architecture
If protected-state access unexpectedly succeeds, qualification fails closed and broader process or PowerShell authority must not proceed
Any ACL repair is limited to Cotra-owned protected state and must not mutate trusted workspace or arbitrary user-file permissions
No executable-registry, PowerShell, network, background, public kill, Git, browser/UI, elevation, or approval authority is added

acceptance.claim: A native Windows provider-private AppContainer fixture attempts to read a Cotra-owned LocalAppData protected-state sentinel and deterministically proves the sentinel contents are inaccessible to the restricted child.
The fixture remains zero-capability AppContainer-contained, is assigned to the kill-on-close Job before resume, and reaches verified Job quiescence after the negative-access probe.
Exact tests prove Cotra/tunnel secret-like environment variables are absent and inherited child handles remain limited to the existing three-handle SG-000009 boundary.
The current request-scoped cotra-mcp to cotrad stdio channel is not passed through PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST or otherwise exposed as process.spawn child authority.

If the default Cotra-owned protected-state ACL permits AppContainer read access, the grain hardens only that Cotra-owned state boundary and native Windows requalification proves denial; no workspace or arbitrary-user-file ACL mutation is introduced.
SG-000009, SG-000009A, SG-000010, and SG-000011 native Windows containment, termination, public-whoami, and descendant-lifecycle regressions remain green.
Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, and security review gates pass with zero unresolved blocking findings.

done_when: Native Windows proves that the restricted process boundary cannot read Cotra-owned protected state or inherit Cotra secret/authority surfaces, any necessary Cotra-owned ACL hardening is merged and requalified, existing process authority does not widen, and implementation receives exact-head plus post-merge verification.
